questions.question: In story S9 (Pending-invitation view, deny layer, caps, accept/decline), is there any vacuous or placeholder production path: a no-op/stub body, a tautological assertion, a frozen stand-in constant, or an optional dependency (injected port, handler, client handle) that silently degrades to non-behavior when not injected? Cite file:line for each injection point in app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/pendingView.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/denyLayer.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/caps.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/acceptDecline.ts; app/src/lib/pendingInvitations.ts (caps constants reused); app/src/lib/blockedPeers.ts (read-only use) and show that omitting the dependency fails loudly rather than succeeding silently.

Could `invitations` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md (imports only via each module's index.ts, no React-context imports under app/src/lib/marmot/**, no ts-mls or @internet-privacy/marmot-ts imports)?

Does S9 comply with the architecture.md boundary rules: only `client/` constructs or disposes the MarmotClient, code inside HistoryBackend calls / inbox handlers / client listeners never awaits an account-scope client call (follow-up work via the owned setTimeout(0) FIFO), group sender identity comes only from orderingKey.account, and idb-keyval update() is not used? List each rule touched by this story's files with file:line evidence, or state why it is not touched.

Do unit, property, and (where the AC names them) library-harness or e2e tests cover the artifacts named in S9's scope (app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/pendingView.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/denyLayer.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/caps.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/acceptDecline.ts; app/src/lib/pendingInvitations.ts (caps constants reused); app/src/lib/blockedPeers.ts (read-only use))? Show that tests use real collaborators or test fixtures rather than mocking the helper used at the SUT call site, that idb mocks are seeded out of key order where order matters, and that at least one test fails if the production code is replaced by a no-op.

Does the delivered S9 implementation match the intent of its scope (invitations.pending() as the only pending store (lp_pendingInvitations_v1 not read/written by new code), ADR-002 pull-only behaviour, native accept/decline (no 21063), blocked-sender drop with decline(id,{declineRumor:false}), 256/8 caps with silent declines, pending view model feeding InvitationCar) and respect its exclusions (Invite-context rumor handler and join-request handler internals (S10, S12) — they consume the deny predicate; UI wiring (S18))? Identify any capability owned by a later story that was built ahead, or any in-scope capability left unimplemented.

Which trust or validation boundaries does S9 touch (signer budget/permissions, relay-supplied events, rumor sender/pubkey attribution, invite/join payloads, privacy invariant that no profile metadata is published to public relays)? Show the validation or defensive check at each boundary with file:line evidence and a test that feeds a malformed or hostile input and observes rejection.

Seam contract PendingInvitationView (consumed beyond S9; consumers: S10): does the delivered artifact at app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/pendingView.ts expose exactly the declared shape (fields: pending: () => PendingInvitation[] (groupId, sponsorAccount, sponsors, id); onChange: (cb) => unsubscribe) and uphold each invariant (invitations.pending() is the only source; lp_pendingInvitations_v1 never read; blocked-sender entries never appear; retained set respects 256 total / 8 per inviter)? Show the type/definition with file:line and a test asserting each invariant, including enum/constant membership and value ranges where the contract constrains them.

Seam contract DenyLayer (consumed beyond S9; consumers: S10): does the delivered artifact at app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/denyLayer.ts expose exactly the declared shape (fields: isBlocked: (pubkey: string) => boolean) and uphold each invariant (blocked sender: nothing stored, no bell; invitation from blocked sender is declined with {declineRumor:false})? Show the type/definition with file:line and a test asserting each invariant, including enum/constant membership and value ranges where the contract constrains them.

AC-INV-2: ADR-002 pull-only: a Welcome from an unrelated sponsor MUST land in `invitations.pending()` and MUST NOT auto-join; the invitee's group list stays unchanged until `accept`. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [harness; e2e:groups-pull-only-invitation-accept (kept)] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-INV-3: Decline: `invitations.decline(id)` MUST remove the invitation from `pending()`, the sponsor's client MUST emit `welcomeDeclined` carrying `inviteeRef`, and the kind-21063 DM MUST NOT be published (recording transport sees no kind-21063). Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [harness; e2e:groups-pull-only-invitation-decline (kept)] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-INV-4: The invitation card MUST render from `invitations.pending()` only; `lp_pendingInvitations_v1` MUST NOT be read or written. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit + structural] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-BLK-1: For a blocked sponsor: an `inboxDisposition: pending` invitation MUST result in no entry in the app pending view, no bell increment, and a call `invitations.decline(id, {declineRumor:false})`; an invite-context rumor and a join request from the same blocked peer MUST each be dropped (nothing stored, no bell). A non-blocked sender MUST be processed normally. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit + harness] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-CAP-1: With 257 pending invitations the 257th MUST be declined (retained total = 256); with 9 from one inviter the 9th MUST be declined (retained per inviter = 8). Declines are silent (no bell, no toast) and made with the library decline. The caps MUST equal the constants of `lib/pendingInvitations.ts` (256 / 8). Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit (stubbed pending list)] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

Library `invitations.decline(id)` sends the decline rumor ONLY when `declineRumor === true` (welcome-processor.js:1050-1078); the default is NO rumor, contrary to marmot-lib-api.md. Confirm acceptDecline.ts passes `{declineRumor:true}` for a user decline (so the sponsor's welcomeDeclined fires, AC-INV-3), pendingView.ts passes `{declineRumor:false}` explicitly for blocked and over-cap entries, and that mutating the user-decline flag to false fails pendingDeny.harness.test.ts (decline test) and the unit decline test.

AC-BLK-1 harness asserts nothing leaves Bob for a blocked sponsor: kind-1059 wrap count equals the count right after the Welcome was published, Alice's client emits no welcomeDeclined within a 600 ms settle window, Bob's library pending() is empty, and the view never announced an arrival; a control sponsor (Carol) in the same run is shown. Confirm the mutation results: forcing `hostile=false` in pendingView.ts fails 5 tests (4 unit + the harness), replacing applyPendingCaps with identity fails 5 (caps unit + view ordering), and flipping the user-decline flag fails 2.

Re-entrancy: pendingView.onInboxDisposition (a client listener) makes no client call and only enqueues scheduleRefresh as its last action; all invitations.pending()/decline() calls run in the queued job or in refresh() called from UI/startup. Verify with pendingView.test.ts 're-entrancy' tests (zero pending() calls before the job runs, triggers collapse into one job) and that the harness wires enqueue to AccountClientHandle.enqueue of a real client with no `reentrant` error (onError throws in the harness).

Caps order: the retained set is the OLDEST invitations (receivedAt asc, tie id), so the 257th arrival / 9th from one inviter is declined and an already shown card is never displaced. The old lp_pendingInvitations_v1 module dropped the OLDEST on overflow; confirm this deliberate inversion matches AC-CAP-1 ('the 257th MUST be declined') and is idempotent (property test over 40 seeded random lists).

`GLOBAL_CAP` / `PER_INVITER_CAP` are now exported from app/src/lib/pendingInvitations.ts and re-exported by caps.ts. S22/S23 delete that module: confirm the sweep story moves the two constants into caps.ts (caps.test.ts asserts equality with the old constants and will then need to assert 256 / 8 literally).
